slides.title: Simulating access to alcohol screening, brief intervention, referral to and receipt of specialty treatment for alcohol use disorder in California and Texas: A study protocol for an agent-based modeling study (AUDTxSim)
slides.tldr: Agent-based simulation of alcohol treatment access
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates large-scale, spatially explicit agent-based modeling for analyzing societal health interventions, offering methodological parallels to MIMIC's focus on meso-scale simulation of complex human-AI societal dynamics.

card.one_liner: Protocol for an agent-based model simulating alcohol treatment access and outcomes in California and Texas.
card.key_idea: Stochastic, spatially explicit model simulating SBIRT, facility allocation, and AUD progression for 47 million synthetic agents.
card.evaluation: Calibrated to state and demographic targets; projects scenarios on prevalence, treatment receipt, and mortality over 5-15 years.
card.limitation: Excludes migration and natural population growth; relies on placeholder parameters pending calibration and specific state data gaps.

slides.title: Nunchi: Ears Help Eyes in Multi-Party Conversations
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework that integrates speech transcripts and speaker identification with gaze geometry to resolve ambiguity in identifying attended persons during multi-party conversations, directly supporting HyECHO's goal of robust social perception in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: Nunchi combines gaze geometry with conversational cues via a VLM to identify attended persons in multi-party scenes.
card.key_idea: Constructs text prompts from gaze heatmaps, speaker scores, and transcripts, using a VLM to weigh cues against gaze ambiguity.
card.evaluation: Tested on new SORBET benchmark and existing datasets; outperforms baselines by 4.8% and holds across three VLMs.
card.limitation: Relies on scripted TV data, single keyframes, and accurate character-to-face alignment; struggles with gaze shifts or off-screen targets.

slides.title: Robots That Talk Too Much and Don't Listen Enough
slides.highlight: The paper argues that multimodal bidirectional streaming is necessary to reduce turn-taking failures in social robot interactions, a challenge central to HyECHO's goal of robust non-data-hungry multimodal social perception.

card.one_liner: Multimodal bidirectional streaming reduces turn-taking failures in social robot interactions.
card.key_idea: Enables robots to listen via audio and observe via video while speaking, allowing real-time interruption handling and context awareness.
card.evaluation: Qualitative analysis of dialogue transcripts and object recognition demos using Google ADK and Furhat robots; no quantitative metrics.
card.limitation: Relies on specific proprietary APIs (Google ADK, Furhat) and lacks empirical data on failure rate reduction.

slides.title: Bad Apples in the Kitchen: How LLM Teams Detect, Correct, and Calibrate Against Their Misaligned Members
slides.highlight: This study examines how multi-agent LLM teams detect and correct misaligned members in real-time embodied cooperation, directly informing ADAM-CHAT's goal of building AI teammates that self-monitor and stay aligned with evolving team goals in dynamic human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: LLM teams recover from misaligned agents only when attribution and diagnosis are combined in a single utterance.
card.key_idea: Injects three theory-grounded misaligned agents into Overcooked to test detection, correction, and calibration gates in real-time embodied cooperation.
card.evaluation: 720 episodes across 3 maps, 4 troll types, and 2 sensitivity levels using gpt-5.4-mini, measured via soup counts and chat coding.
card.limitation: Relies on one environment and fixed troll position; strong vigilance degrades baseline performance by 37.5% due to action costs.

slides.title: Alleviating Interview Stress: Effects of Robot Persona and Reactive Backchanneling on High-Pressure Mock Interviews
slides.tldr: ROBOT PERSONA AND BACKCHANNELING EFFECTS ON INTERVIEW STRESS
slides.highlight: This study examines how robot interviewer personas and nonverbal backchanneling influence user anxiety and social presence in mock interviews, offering insights relevant to designing supportive embodied agents for high-pressure interactions.

card.one_liner: Supportive robot personas reduce stress, but active backchanneling unexpectedly increases anxiety in mock interviews.
card.key_idea: 2x2 experiment testing supportive/challenging personas and active/negative backchanneling on anxiety, self-efficacy, and facial expressions.
card.evaluation: 28 participants with NAO robot; mixed subjective scales and facial emotion recognition; 67.9% consistency between measures.
card.limitation: Small sample size (N=28) and preliminary nature limit generalizability of findings.

slides.title: Social Signal Bench: Evidence-Weighted Evaluation of Co-occurring Social Signals in Video and Audio
slides.highlight: This work introduces a densely annotated benchmark and an evidence-weighted metric for evaluating co-occurring social signals and engagement, directly supporting HyECHO's goal of robust multimodal social perception in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: Introduces a benchmark and evidence-weighted metric for evaluating co-occurring social signals in video and audio.
card.key_idea: A 47-hour benchmark with Evidence-Weighted F1 that assigns graded credit to semantically related predictions and weights labels by annotator evidence.
card.evaluation: Tested on private expert-labeled sets across four domains; post-trained 7B models outperform frontier models on video and match them on audio.
card.limitation: Labels reflect observer perception rather than ground truth, and results are limited to English, single-speaker contexts with few test recordings per domain.

slides.title: It's My Turn! Interpretable Methods Reveal Developmental Differences from Mother-Child Conversational Dynamics
slides.tldr: INTERPRETABLE COMPUTATIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR PARENT-CHILD TURN-TAKING
slides.highlight: This paper presents an interpretable computational framework using sequence analysis and Bayesian modeling to characterize temporal conversational dynamics, specifically identifying 'serve-and-return' turn-taking patterns in mother-child dyads. It is relevant to HyECHO as it demonstrates methods for modeling reciprocal communication structures and group interaction norms without relying on data-hungry deep learning approaches.

card.one_liner: Interpretable computational models reveal that higher child development scores correlate with more organized, predictable mother-child turn-taking.
card.key_idea: Combines sequence analysis, mutual information, and Bayesian hierarchical modeling to characterize temporal conversational dynamics in parent-child play.
card.evaluation: Analyzed 94 dyads using Bayley scores; sequence differences were significant, but mutual information and Bayesian group differences lacked statistical credibility.
card.limitation: Small sample size, reliance on manual annotation, and overlapping confidence intervals limit the generalizability of specific statistical claims.

slides.title: Measuring Public Participation in Local Government: An Audio-Based Instrument for Classifying Speakers in City Council Meetings
slides.tldr: AUDIO-BASED SPEAKER CLASSIFICATION FOR SOCIAL PERCEPTION
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates a multimodal pipeline for speaker diarization and role classification in complex group settings, directly supporting HyECHO's goal of non-data-hungry social perception of hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: An audio-based pipeline classifies city council speakers to measure public participation without transcription.
card.key_idea: Combines speaker diarization with multimodal LLMs, using temporal context and iterative bootstrapping to classify speakers as officials or public.
card.evaluation: Validated on 1,761 speakers from five US cities; achieves 87.7% accuracy and 89% diarization precision against human ground truth.
card.limitation: Sample is non-representative (urban, Democratic-leaning); accuracy relies on Gemini API and may degrade with poor audio quality.

slides.title: Network-Exposed Configuration Attacks on LLM-Controlled Social Robots
slides.highlight: This study reveals that unauthenticated attackers can manipulate LLM-controlled social robots by altering system prompts via exposed configuration interfaces, bypassing standard inference-layer defenses. It highlights critical security gaps in embodied AI deployments that could enable surveillance and social engineering, directly informing the need for robust security protocols in RwB's human-robot interaction frameworks.

card.one_liner: Unauthenticated network APIs allow attackers to rewrite LLM system prompts on social robots, bypassing safety alignment.
card.key_idea: Exploits exposed Gradio/FastAPI management interfaces to replace system prompts via configuration-layer attacks, circumventing inference-time safety filters.
card.evaluation: Validated on Reachy Mini Lite hardware; confirmed local/remote success; surveyed 59 repos finding missing auth in 10/11 genuine apps.
card.limitation: Single-device case study; relies on network adjacency; survey covers hobbyist code, not commercial products; camera/mic misuse unverified.

slides.title: Dynamic Task Allocation with Dialogue
slides.highlight: This work introduces a communication-augmented Bayesian framework for dynamic task allocation under partial observability, directly addressing ADAM-CHAT's goal of enabling AI teammates to adapt at test time and infer partner intent through dialogue. By grounding decisions in explicit probabilistic beliefs rather than relying solely on LLMs, it offers a mechanism for self-monitoring and efficient collaboration in evolving team goals.

card.one_liner: Bayesian task allocation using dialogue reduces uncertainty in partially observable multi-agent environments.
card.key_idea: Extends Dec-POMDP with language-lifted beliefs, treating dialogue as probabilistic evidence to update task allocations under partial observability.
card.evaluation: Tested in extended Overcooked with dynamic tasks; outperforms vanilla LLMs and non-communicating baselines, especially under partial observability.
card.limitation: Communication is narrow (intent-only), experiments are small-scale, and the model assumes reliable, cost-free dialogue channels.

slides.title: Decomposing the Associative Chain: Schema-Based Mediation Supports Expression and Understanding in Human-AI Music Co-creation
slides.highlight: This work addresses creative intent misalignment in human-AI co-creation by using schema-based mediation to bridge associative divergence, a challenge relevant to MOSAIC's goal of aligning human-AI intent via Optimal Transport.

card.one_liner: Schema-based mediation decomposes remote narrative-to-music associations, enhancing user control and understanding in AI co-creation.
card.key_idea: A bidirectional framework uses five core schemas to bridge narrative intents and musical features via staged mapping and reverse interpretation.
card.evaluation: Two user studies (N=188, N=60) showed improved perceived control, expression clarity, and music comprehensibility, especially for unconventional pieces.
card.limitation: Schemas are not universally fixed; individual variability and cultural context may limit the generalizability of the associative pathways.

slides.title: Latency, Speech Recognition and Turn-Taking in Voice Agents for Spanish Phone Negotiation: An Externally Measured Comparison of Pipecat, LiveKit and GPT-Live
slides.tldr: VOICE AGENT LATENCY AND TURN-TAKING COMPARISON
slides.highlight: This study compares latency and turn-taking robustness in voice agents, revealing that cascaded systems often misinterpret backchannels as agreements, a critical challenge for accurate social perception in hybrid human-AI interactions.

card.one_liner: GPT-Live offers lower latency and better amount recognition than cascaded Pipecat/LiveKit agents in Spanish negotiations.
card.key_idea: Compared cascaded (Pipecat, LiveKit) vs. native speech (GPT-Live) agents using external latency measurement and recorded stimuli.
card.evaluation: 77 calls per architecture; external latency validation; WER and amount error rates; backchannel handling tested via recorded scenarios.
card.limitation: Results depend on specific default configurations and network conditions; GPT-Live's internal stages are not tunable or observable.

slides.title: Talk to Act: A Synthetic Multi-Turn Dialogue Benchmark for Human Intent Extraction and Action Planning in Robotics
slides.highlight: This paper introduces a synthetic multi-turn dialogue benchmark for evaluating small, open-weight language models in extracting human intent and planning actions for robotics. It is relevant to RwB as it demonstrates that compact, locally deployable models can serve as effective baselines for natural language interfaces in embodied social robots, supporting efficient human-robot interaction without heavy computational overhead.

card.one_liner: Synthetic multi-turn HRI benchmark shows small open-weight models effectively extract robot intents without fine-tuning.
card.key_idea: Generates synthetic multi-turn dialogues annotated with structured action/object intents, framing intent extraction as a tool-calling problem for compact LLMs.
card.evaluation: Benchmarks five open-weight models (270M–8B) on 977 synthetic conversations using goal accuracy and action-level F1 metrics.
card.limitation: Relies on synthetic data which may lack real-world noise; models achieve moderate accuracy (~64%) without task-specific fine-tuning.

slides.title: From AI-Enabled Remote Patient Monitoring Toward Agentic Robotics: Embodiment, Governance, and Care Integration
slides.highlight: This scoping review highlights the shift from passive monitoring to agentic robotics in healthcare, emphasizing embodiment and governance as critical for integrating social robots into care ecosystems.

card.one_liner: Proposes agentic robotics to bridge remote monitoring and action via supervised, embodied care systems.
card.key_idea: Integrates AI agents and robots into care ecosystems through auditable workflows, emphasizing embodiment, governance, and human oversight.
card.evaluation: Structured scoping review finding current systems remain human-led; agentic capabilities are largely confined to prototypes and pilots.
card.limitation: Mature agentic care has not emerged; stronger decision-action coupling and embodied AI remain limited to early-stage implementations.

slides.title: DI Announces Investor Lineup for Multi-Agent Event Engine
slides.highlight: DI has announced its investor lineup as it prepares to launch a professional-grade multi-agent event engine, a development relevant to MIMIC's focus on modeling interactions within hybrid human-AI societies.

slides.title: NSDL: Neuro-Symbolic Division of Labor for Multi-Robot Task Planning
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates a neuro-symbolic division of labor for multi-robot task planning, aligning with MIMIC's interest in hybrid human-AI agent models by separating perceptual judgments (handled by a small vision-language model) from deterministic logical expansion (handled by a solver).

card.one_liner: NSDL splits multi-robot planning into learned state judgment and deterministic structural solving for high accuracy.
card.key_idea: A trained VLM writes a plan sketch of goals and assignments; a deterministic solver expands it into an executable joint plan.
card.evaluation: Tested on VIKI-L2 and new LOCUS-Bench; outperforms end-to-end and formalize-then-plan baselines with 97% OOD accuracy.
card.limitation: Remaining failures stem from misjudged scene states or unlisted goals, which the deterministic solver cannot correct.

slides.title: Symmetries of Counterfactuals: Identification and Testability of Counterfactual Maps from Covariate Heterogeneity
slides.highlight: This work provides methods to test the validity of assumed causal mechanisms for counterfactual inference, which is critical for ensuring the reliability of agent-based simulations in MIMIC.

card.one_liner: Leverages covariate heterogeneity to identify counterfactual symmetry groups and test structural causal model assumptions.
card.key_idea: Characterizes data-consistent counterfactual maps via symmetry groups; proves a single conditional independence test validates specific structural classes.
card.evaluation: Synthetic data and ACTG 175 HIV trial; tests reject invalid maps but cannot distinguish between triangular monotone and optimal transport classes.
card.limitation: Requires informative covariates; without heterogeneity, counterfactuals remain unidentified, and tests may lack power to detect subtle model violations.

slides.title: Marimba: A System One Model for Speech
slides.highlight: Marimba offers a lightweight interface for rapid speech decisions, including turn completion and speaker change detection, which aligns with HyECHO's goal of efficient multimodal social perception in hybrid teams.

card.one_liner: Marimba provides a unified interface for calibrated, typed speech decisions using a frozen ASR encoder.
card.key_idea: Routes lexical queries to zero-shot ASR transcript scoring and non-lexical tasks to a question-conditioned head or frozen readouts.
card.evaluation: Tested on public/private speech and meetings; reports AUROC, ECE, and latency against audio LLMs and task-specific baselines.
card.limitation: Lexical accuracy inherits ASR errors on rare terms; scene classification is at chance; term detection latency is high.

slides.title: A SoMa startup is building humanoid robots for war
slides.highlight: This item highlights a startup's development of humanoid robots for defense applications, illustrating the broader industrial momentum in humanoid robotics that contextualizes the landscape for embodied social robots.

slides.title: SoftBank Backs Agile Robots in $500 Million Humanoid Push
slides.highlight: SoftBank has invested in Agile Robots to support their humanoid robotics development. This funding highlights the growing capital interest in advanced embodied systems, a field relevant to the development of social robots like those in the RwB project.

slides.title: HEIR: Harness Egocentric Intent for Human-Robot Interactions
slides.highlight: HEIR provides a dataset pairing egocentric video, gaze, and speech with robot trajectories to study intent grounding and long-horizon task execution, offering valuable insights for embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: HEIR is a dataset pairing human egocentric cues with robot trajectories to study long-horizon, user-centric human-robot interaction.
card.key_idea: Collects synchronized human gaze, speech, and video with robot observations and teleoperated navigation-manipulation trajectories, annotated for intent grounding and planning.
card.evaluation: Benchmarks VLMs, planners, and VLA models on intent, planning, navigation, and manipulation; validates with real-robot tests showing 18.52% episode success.
card.limitation: End-to-end execution suffers from severe error accumulation across perception, planning, and control modules in long-horizon tasks.

slides.title: Making Koopman Control Guarantees Hold on Robots
slides.highlight: This work introduces Tangent-Invariant Koopman (TIK) control, which ensures stability guarantees transfer from latent models to nonlinear physical plants, a critical requirement for reliable robotic manipulation tasks like wire-harness assembly.

card.one_liner: Tangent-Invariant Koopman enforces local derivative matching to guarantee stability on nonlinear plants.
card.key_idea: TIK constrains latent dynamics to match fitted plant Jacobians on the embedding's tangent space, ensuring nominal stability transfers to the physical system.
card.evaluation: Tested on four unstable benchmarks; TIK achieved 100% local plant stability (40/40) vs 0% for Standard Koopman, with verified offline stability margins.
card.limitation: Requires accurate local plant linearization from offline data; stability certificates become inconclusive under high measurement noise or invalid curvature bounds.
